summary: The extremal reduction and terminal triangle calculation address only configurations with p_3<Q. They do not exclude p_3=Q, so the proof establishes at most the non-strict conclusion p_3\ge Q rather than the stated strict conclusion p_3>Q.
critical_errors: The contradiction setup (5) assumes p_3(K_0)<Q, but a violation of the claimed implication p_1,p_2<M implies p_3>Q can have p_3=Q. Such a counterexample does not enter the negative sublevel argument. The same issue occurs in the final Hausdorff approximation: when the limiting body has p_3=Q, nearby polygons need not satisfy p_3<Q. Thus the assertions that the argument proves (1) for polygons and then for all convex bodies do not follow.
gaps: No perturbation or separate equality-case argument is supplied to convert a putative configuration with p_3=Q and p_1,p_2<M into one with p_3<Q.
repair_hints: Add and justify a small-translation argument: translate the body by t v with \ell_3(v)>0. Because O is interior, the section on \ell_3=0 has positive length, so p_3 strictly decreases for small t>0; O remains interior and the strict margins p_1,p_2<M persist by continuity. Apply this before the polygonal contradiction, and likewise before approximation in the general-body case.
